# Pitloom's catalogued messages: Targets

See also: `messages.md` (the index of every code), `../SKILL.md` (which holds
the rule: explain and relay, never run the fix).

Trust a code only when the line is one of the lines below, a value in place of
each `<name>`, after at most one prefix: the index lists the prefixes and
`messages-values.md` the values.

### `config-unsafe`

- **Level**: INFO.
- **Means**: The [tool.pitloom] settings of a project fetched from a Git URL, or
  of an sdist downloaded from a PyPI URL, if it has any, are not applied: they
  could point Pitloom at files, a registry or the network as the project
  chooses, and the project is untrusted.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Did not apply them: the run uses Pitloom's defaults, or the
  settings of --config (pitloom_config= in the library) when given, which also
  silences this line.
- **Nothing to do**: the SBOM is generated with the defaults; settings the user
  trusts go in a file they pass with --config.
- **Printed after**: `Git source: <text>` (a Git URL fetch), on its INFO lines;
  the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  INFO: the repository's own [tool.pitloom] settings are ignored (untrusted); --config or pitloom_config= applies [config-unsafe]
  INFO: FILE=<file>: the downloaded sdist's own [tool.pitloom] settings are ignored (untrusted); --config or pitloom_config= applies [config-unsafe]
  ```

- **Since**: 0.23.4; line 1: 0.25.0

### `config-unsafe/build-code`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: The build configuration of a project fetched from a Git URL names
  Python code of the repository that listing the wheel's files would run: a
  Hatchling metadata hook, a setuptools cmdclass or attr version, a PDM build
  hook (pdm_build.py or custom-hook) or run-setuptools; or a setup.cfg [global]
  section, which sets setuptools' own options (where it reads files from, which
  command code it loads). The repository is untrusted, so that code is not run
  and those options are not set. The line names the file that holds the settings
  and the settings ignored.
- **SBOM effect**: weaker: what the SBOM says is less sure.
- **Pitloom did**: Ignored those settings: no code of the repository ran, and
  the wheel's files were listed from the rest of the build configuration, which
  may miss a file that code would add.
- **Tell the user**: that the repository's build configuration names code that
  Pitloom does not run on a downloaded repository, so the file list may miss
  what it would add. To have it, they clone the repository, review that code,
  and generate from the local copy. Do not clone or run that code for them; ask
  first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: build-time code of the downloaded repository is not run; <settings> ignored [config-unsafe/build-code]
  ```

### `hf-url-invalid`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A Hugging Face target is neither a Hub model URL
  (https://huggingface.co/<owner>/<name>) nor a model id (<owner>/<name>).
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Read nothing and sent no request: 'loom model', 'loom
  project' and 'loom generate' exit 1; generate, generate_model_sbom,
  generate_project_sbom, generate_git_project_sbom and read_huggingface raise
  ValueError carrying the code. An http(s) URL on huggingface.co or hf.co that
  is no Space or dataset is taken as a model URL, so a malformed one says this,
  not that a model file is not found.
- **Tell the user**: the URL or id was not read, as the line gives it. They
  check it and run again. Do not guess another model and run for them; ask
  first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: URL=<url>: not a valid Hugging Face URL or model ID [hf-url-invalid]
  ```

### `input-not-found`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A path named for Pitloom to read does not exist: a model file,
  wheel, sdist, project directory, configuration, ID registry or SBOM file, or a
  PATH given to 'loom id generate' to index, on disk (or something else is
  there: the line says it is not a file, or not a directory), the file or
  directory a Git URL names in the repository at its branch (a symbolic link
  there is not followed, so it counts as absent: its line says it is a link), or
  a pattern or directory that holds nothing of what was asked for (or a wheel
  pattern nested too deeply to expand: its line says so).
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Wrote nothing: no SBOM is written; for 'loom id', the ID
  registry is not written; for 'loom embed-wheel', no wheel is changed; a check
  ('loom fragment validate', 'loom verify-wheel', 'loom validate-wheel') checks
  nothing. The command exits 1 (the Action step fails), the build hook fails the
  build, and the library raises FileNotFoundError carrying the code
  (IdRegistry.generate for a path to index that is not there), ValueError for a
  fragments directory that holds no JSON file, or RemoteSourceError (code
  git.path-not-found) for a Git URL's file or directory. As a WARNING, an ID
  registry file was gone (or no longer a file) when a run whose SBOM is already
  built read it again to save the ids it added: nothing is saved and the SBOM
  stands.
- **Tell the user**: which path was not found, as the line names it (for a Git
  URL, a path in the repository). They check the path, or the URL's branch and
  path, and run again. Do not guess another path or branch and run for them; ask
  first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: no file '<path>' in the repository at that branch [input-not-found]
  ERROR: file '<path>' in the repository at that branch is a symbolic link; links are not followed [input-not-found]
  ERROR: no directory '<path>' in the repository at that branch [input-not-found]
  ERROR: <input> not found: '<path>' [input-not-found]
  ERROR: <input> not found: '<path>' is not a file [input-not-found]
  ERROR: <input> not found: '<path>' is not a directory [input-not-found]
  ERROR: no wheel file matches '<path>' [input-not-found]
  ERROR: no wheel file matches '<path>': the pattern nests too deeply to expand; name each wheel file without a pattern [input-not-found]
  ERROR: no JSON fragment file in '<path>' [input-not-found]
  ERROR: no source or data directory under '<path>'; pass PATH arguments [input-not-found]
  WARNING: <input> not found: '<path>' [input-not-found]
  WARNING: <input> not found: '<path>' is not a file [input-not-found]
  ```

- **Since**: 0.23.4; lines 1-12: 0.25.0

### `input-not-found/fragment`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: An SBOM fragment the project configures ([tool.pitloom.fragment])
  does not exist.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Merged the SBOM without it, and wrote it (the build hook
  builds the wheel). For a fragment marked required, the merge then fails with
  fragment-missing and no SBOM is written: the command exits 1, the hook fails
  the build, the library raises FragmentMergeError. 'loom fragment list' lists
  it with EXISTS=false, and exits 1 for a required one.
- **Tell the user**: which fragment was not found, as the line names it. They
  create it (run the enrichment that writes it), fix its path in the
  configuration, or remove the entry, and run again. Do not edit the
  configuration for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: SBOM fragment not found; not merged [input-not-found/fragment]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: SBOM fragment not found; required, so the merge will fail [input-not-found/fragment]
  ```

### `model-ambiguous`

- **Level**: ERROR, INFO. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A directory named for an AI model SBOM holds several AI model
  files, and no file was named: one SBOM describes one model.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Wrote no SBOM. One INFO line per model file found names it,
  in sorted order, before the error.
- **Tell the user**: which model files the directory holds, as the INFO lines
  name them. They name the one they want (its path, or for a Git URL the link to
  the file's page) and generate again, once per model. Do not pick a file and
  generate for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  INFO: FILE=<file>: one of several AI model files [model-ambiguous]
  ERROR: '<path>': several AI model files<count>; name one file [model-ambiguous]
  ```

### `model-ambiguous/over-cap`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A directory named for an AI model SBOM holds more files whose names
  could be AI models than its cap, and no file was named: which of them are
  models is not known, and one SBOM describes one model.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Wrote no SBOM; no file of the directory was read, said first
  in one over-cap WARNING.
- **Tell the user**: the directory holds too many files that could be models for
  Pitloom to look at. They name the one model file they want (its path, or for a
  Git URL the link to the file's page), or a directory holding only it, and
  generate again. Do not pick a file and generate for them; ask first, and with
  nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: '<path>': more than <limit> files that could be AI models, none read; name one file [model-ambiguous/over-cap]
  ```

### `project-not-found`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A directory read as a Python project holds no project config
  (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or setup.py).
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Wrote no SBOM. Subdirectories are not searched; for a Git URL
  whose subdirectories hold a project, the line names them (git.no-project).
- **Tell the user**: the directory holds no Python project, as the line names
  it. They name the project's directory (for a monorepo, the sub-project's
  directory the error names, if any) and generate again. Do not guess a
  directory and generate for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it
  only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: '<path>': no Python project (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or setup.py) [project-not-found]
  ERROR: '<path>': no Python project (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or setup.py); Python projects are in subdirectories (<directories>); give the URL of one of them [project-not-found]
  ERROR: '<path>': no Python project (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or setup.py); Python projects are in subdirectories (<directories>); Pitloom reads the directory in the URL only [project-not-found]
  ```

- **Since**: 0.23.4; lines 1-3: 0.25.0

### `project-not-found/model-files`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A project SBOM was asked for a directory of a Git URL that holds no
  Python project (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or setup.py) but files whose names
  could be AI models.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Wrote no SBOM; no file was read. The error code is
  git.no-project.
- **Tell the user**: the directory has no project but may hold AI models, as the
  line names them. For a model SBOM they run loom model or loom generate on the
  same URL (generate_git_sbom in the library). Do not run it for them; ask
  first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: '<path>': no Python project (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or setup.py); it holds files that may be AI models (<files>): use 'loom model <url>' or 'loom generate <url>' [project-not-found/model-files]
  ERROR: '<path>': no Python project (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or setup.py); it holds files that may be AI models (<files>): use generate_git_sbom(url, sbom_kind='model') or generate(url) [project-not-found/model-files]
  ```

- **Since**: 0.23.4; lines 1-2: 0.25.0

### `project-or-model-not-found`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A directory named for an SBOM holds neither a Python project
  (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or setup.py) nor, directly in it, an AI model file
  of a supported format.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Wrote no SBOM. Subdirectories are not searched for a model
  file; for a Git URL whose subdirectories hold a project, the line names them.
- **Tell the user**: the directory has no project and no model file Pitloom
  reads. They name the project's directory, or the model file itself (its path,
  or for a Git URL the link to the file's page), and generate again. Do not
  guess a file or directory and generate for them; ask first, and with nobody to
  ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: '<path>': no Python project (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or setup.py) and no AI model file of a supported format; name a project directory or a model file [project-or-model-not-found]
  ERROR: '<path>': no Python project (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or setup.py) and no AI model file of a supported format; Python projects are in subdirectories (<directories>); give the URL of one of them [project-or-model-not-found]
  ERROR: '<path>': no Python project (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or setup.py) and no AI model file of a supported format; Python projects are in subdirectories (<directories>); Pitloom reads the directory in the URL only [project-or-model-not-found]
  ```

- **Since**: 0.23.4; lines 1-3: 0.25.0

### `sbom-invalid`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: An SBOM given to read is JSON but not a valid SPDX 3 document: its
  @graph is not a list of objects ('embed-wheel --sbom', 'loom id import';
  checked before the format, whatever the file is named), an object of it names
  one key twice (JSON readers disagree on which value counts, so what was
  checked may not be what is embedded), the SPDX 3 reader refuses it ('loom id
  import': an object with no type, a property of the wrong kind; the reader's
  text after the line's ';'), or spdx3-validate refuses it ('embed-wheel --sbom
  --validate', 'loom validate-wheel', 'loom fragment validate': its findings
  come before, each line after spdx3-validate: , then one line per document, or
  for the documents merged; a document it could not load says why the same way).
  As a WARNING: 'loom id import' into an empty registry finds a document id that
  cannot be a namespace: not an absolute IRI, holding '#', or holding a
  character an IRI cannot hold (a space).
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Wrote nothing: no wheel is changed, no ID is imported. The
  command exits 1 ('loom validate-wheel' reports the wheel failed and goes on
  with the next); the library (embed_wheel_sbom with sbom_path,
  IdRegistry.import_sbom) raises ValueError carrying the code for an @graph that
  is not a list of objects, a key given twice or an SBOM the SPDX 3 reader
  refuses. As a WARNING, the import goes on and the registry keeps the namespace
  it was created with.
- **Tell the user**: which SBOM is not valid, and what the validator reported.
  They fix or regenerate it and run again. Do not edit the SBOM for them; ask
  first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: SBOM is not valid; no wheel was written [sbom-invalid]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: SBOM @graph is not a list [sbom-invalid]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: SBOM @graph holds an element that is not an object [sbom-invalid]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: SBOM holds an object with a key given twice [sbom-invalid]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: SBOM cannot be read as SPDX 3; <failure> [sbom-invalid]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: SBOM namespace <why>; the ID registry keeps its own, not <namespace> [sbom-invalid]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: not valid SPDX 3 (<number> finding(s) above) [sbom-invalid]
  ERROR: the SBOMs together are not valid SPDX 3 (<number> finding(s) above) [sbom-invalid]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: could not be validated; spdx3-validate says why above [sbom-invalid]
  ERROR: the SBOMs could not be validated; spdx3-validate says why above [sbom-invalid]
  ```

### `sbom-wrong-format`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: An SBOM given to embed or to import into an ID registry is named as
  SPDX 3 JSON-LD (.spdx3.json) but holds another format (a CycloneDX document,
  say).
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Wrote nothing: no wheel is changed and no ID registry
  written; the command exits 1, the library raises ValueError carrying the code.
- **Tell the user**: which file is named as SPDX 3 but is not, as the line names
  it. They give the right file, or rename it to match its format, and run again.
  Do not rename or convert the file for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask,
  report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: named .spdx3.json but not SPDX 3 JSON-LD [sbom-wrong-format]
  ```

### `target-ambiguous`

- **Level**: INFO.
- **Means**: The path named for an SBOM is a directory, or a file in it whose
  name no AI model file has and that is not one, or is missing (a Git URL of
  README.md), so it does not say by itself what the SBOM describes; Pitloom
  decided by the rule: a project config makes it a project's, else the
  directory's one AI model file is read.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Read what the line names: the directory, or its one model
  file. The SBOM describes that file, or the directory's project.
- **Nothing to do**: the SBOM describes what the line names; to describe another
  file of the directory, name that file.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  INFO: FILE=<file>: not an AI model file; reading its directory [target-ambiguous]
  INFO: FILE=<file>: no Python project; reading this AI model file [target-ambiguous]
  INFO: FILE=<file>: the one AI model file; reading it [target-ambiguous]
  ```

- **Since**: 0.23.4; line 1: 0.25.0

### `target-ambiguous/git-page`

- **Level**: INFO.
- **Means**: A Git URL names more than a repository, or names it in another
  spelling: a web page of a repository (with a branch, tag or commit, a
  directory or a file), a URL that is not itself a repository's, or a page of a
  file that is a directory (or of a directory that is a file). Pitloom decided
  by its rule what the URL names.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Read what the line names: the repository, at the branch, tag
  or commit, and the directory or file, it names.
- **Nothing to do**: the SBOM describes what the line names; to describe another
  version or directory, give its URL.
- **Printed after**: `Git source: <text>` (a Git URL fetch), on its INFO lines;
  the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  INFO: URL=<url>: read as repository <target> [target-ambiguous/git-page]
  INFO: URL=<url>: read as repository <target>, <ref-kind> <ref> [target-ambiguous/git-page]
  INFO: URL=<url>: read as repository <target>, directory '<path>' [target-ambiguous/git-page]
  INFO: URL=<url>: read as repository <target>, <ref-kind> <ref>, directory '<path>' [target-ambiguous/git-page]
  INFO: URL=<url>: not a repository; read as repository <target> [target-ambiguous/git-page]
  INFO: URL=<url>: '<path>' is a file, not a directory; read as the file named [target-ambiguous/git-page]
  INFO: URL=<url>: '<path>' is a directory, not a file; reading it [target-ambiguous/git-page]
  ```

### `target-ambiguous/hf-url`

- **Level**: INFO.
- **Means**: A Hugging Face model URL spelt otherwise than
  https://huggingface.co/<owner>/<name> (hf.co, www.huggingface.co, http://, a
  scheme or host in another case). Pitloom decided by its rule which model it
  names.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Read the model the line names, from the Hub the run asks
  (https://huggingface.co unless HF_ENDPOINT names another).
- **Nothing to do**: the SBOM describes the model the line names; to describe
  another, give its URL.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  INFO: URL=<url>: read as Hugging Face model <target> [target-ambiguous/hf-url]
  ```

### `target-wrong-format`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: The target given is not of the kind the command reads: a Hugging
  Face model given to 'loom project', or a file not named .whl given as a wheel
  ('loom wheel', 'embed-wheel', 'verify-wheel', 'validate-wheel').
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Read nothing of it: the command exits 1; the library raises
  ValueError carrying the code (generate_project_sbom and
  generate_git_project_sbom for a Hugging Face model URL, generate_wheel_sbom
  for a file not named .whl).
- **The caller may fix**: The caller may run the command the line names, or give
  a wheel file (a built .whl), and run again.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: URL=<url>: a Hugging Face model, not a project; use 'loom model' [target-wrong-format]
  ERROR: URL=<url>: a Hugging Face model, not a project; use generate_model_sbom() [target-wrong-format]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: not a .whl file [target-wrong-format]
  ```
